verbatim: In February, the company announced that the FDA has approved Breyanzi (lisocabtagene maraleucel: liso-cel), a CD19-directed CAR T cell therapy for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory (R/R) large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL) after two or more lines of systemic therapy, including diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) not otherwise specified (including DLBCL arising from indolent lymphoma), high-grade B-cell lymphoma, primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma, and follicular lymphoma grade 3B.
source_doc: Bristol Myers Squibb Reports First Quarter Financial Results for 2021 (press release, Form 8-K exhibit 99.1, 29 Apr 2021)
notes: Breyanzi has no row in the Q1 2021 product revenue table; first revenue reported in Q2 2021 (USD 17m, all U.S.).

verbatim: The FDA approved Breyanzi for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma
source_doc: Bristol Myers Squibb Reports Second Quarter Financial Results for 2022 (press release, Form 8-K exhibit 99.1, 27 Jul 2022)
notes: Second-line LBCL approval (June 2022), headline: 'Strengthens Cell Therapy Franchise with Broadest Label for Breyanzi in Relapsed or Refractory Large B-cell Lymphoma after One Prior Therapy'. EC approval of the third-line indication was reported in the Q1 2022 release.

verbatim: U.S. Approval of Breyanzi in Both Follicular Lymphoma and Mantle Cell Lymphoma
source_doc: Bristol Myers Squibb Reports Second Quarter Financial Results for 2024 (press release, Form 8-K exhibit 99.1, 26 Jul 2024)
notes: Label expansions in Q2 2024 (FL and MCL); CLL accelerated approval reported in the Q1 2024 release. These coincide with the step-up in 2024 revenue.

verbatim: The FDA approved label updates for CAR T cell therapies Breyanzi and Abecma that reduce certain patient monitoring requirements and remove the Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) programs that were in place since each product was initially approved.
source_doc: Bristol Myers Squibb Reports Second Quarter Financial Results for 2025 (press release, Form 8-K exhibit 99.1, 31 Jul 2025)
notes: REMS removal (June 2025) relevant to site expansion / access.

verbatim: The FDA approved Breyanzi as the first and only CAR T treatment for adult patients with relapsed or refractory marginal zone lymphoma who have received at least two prior lines.
